paper_title: NExtLong Toward Effective Long-Context Training without Long Documents
caption: NExtLong reduces the model's dependence on proximal text. We calculated the degree of dependence on proximal text (the last third of the text) for different methods when completing the LongQA task. It can be observed that NExtLong significantly reduces the model's dependence on proximal text.
model_annotation: The vertical bar chart illustrates the Short-Dependence Attention Weight across five different methods. The horizontal axis contains the categories, labeled "Methods", and displays the categories from left to right in the following order: Standard, ICLM, KNN, Quest, and NExtLong, with the label text tilted diagonally. The vertical axis is the value axis, labeled "Attention Weight", utilizing a linear scale with a displayed range from 0.80 to 0.90 and major numeric tick labels spaced evenly at intervals of 0.02. The tallest bar corresponds to the Standard method, reaching a value of approximately 0.865. The remaining bars indicate values of approximately 0.864 for KNN, 0.863 for Quest, and 0.854 for ICLM. The shortest bar represents the NExtLong method, which drops to an approximate value of 0.827. The categories are not sorted in a specific ascending, descending, or alphabetical order, and no individual bars are visually emphasized through contrasting colors, outlines, or annotations. A thin gray grid overlays the background, aligning with both the vertical value ticks and the center of each horizontal category.
